hypothesis: K-405 / PLAYBOOK P-2.2 -- magnitude is the responder: does a LOCAL b estimated only from the past forecast the size distribution of the next events better than one global b?
success_rule: gain > 0.02 bits/event with the 95%% sequence-block CI excluding 0, on BOTH catalogues
named_observer_artifact: spatial/temporal Mc variation masquerading as b variation; controls (a) +0.3 floor raise, (b) measured native magnitude binning, (c) M>=2.5 subset above the diurnal-detection band

control_b_native_binwidth.note: same 0.1-mag Mc/b estimator, likelihood bins at the measured native magnitude resolution

merton_lilliefors_exponentiality.reference: Herrmann & Marzocchi (2021): QTM and SCSN SoCal are only Lilliefors-complete near M 3.24, i.e. magnitudes are NOT exponential down to a maximum-curvature floor.

sensitivity.note: b(x) = 1.0 +/- delta linear in longitude, injected above (global Mc - 0.5) into a magnitude-shuffled catalogue; identical pipeline. delta=0 is the false-positive check.

QTM_12dev.txt.defensible_floor_statement: The relative log-score comparison (local b vs global b, identical support) is fair at any floor. The b-VALUE interpretation is defensible only above the Lilliefors floor measured here (2.6000000000000005); at the maximum-curvature floor (M 0.2) the magnitude distribution of this catalogue is not exponential, so 'b' is a two-parameter summary of a non-GR distribution, not a Gutenberg-Richter slope.
